name: The Reclamation Loan: Cadrex Built the Gray Zone to Stay
description: When GLMZ's lower districts were formally rezoned as 'Tier 1 Reclamation Zones' in 2191 under the Infrastructure Renewal Compact, Cadrex Urban Solutions was awarded the development contract to rebuild the Gray Zone housing as upwardly mobile Tier 2 stock within fifteen years. The conspiracy — now treated as near-fact in many the Gray Zone communities — holds that Cadrex deliberately designed the Reclamation housing with structural obsolescence built in: materials certified for twenty-year lifespans that began degrading within eight, utility hookups incompatible with Tier 2 grid standards, and zoning classifications quietly reclassified to prevent resale upward. The goal, believers argue, was to keep the Gray Zone population captive as a permanent low-cost labor reserve and consumer base for Cadrex's own the Gray Zone-tier commercial subsidiaries.
cultural_impact: Anti-Cadrex sentiment is nearly universal in the Gray Zone, and Cadrex logos are among the most common targets for graffiti modification by the Gray Zone art collectives. The phrase 'Cadrex concrete' has become the Gray Zone slang for anything designed to appear functional while ensuring dependency.
key_figures: the Gray Zone organizer Tomoko Adeyemi-Cruz
locations: Cadrex Regional HQ, Tier 3 South Loop
The Wall of Receipts (the Gray Zone community documentation mural, Lower Cuyahoga)
story_hooks: A the Gray Zone building collapses ahead of schedule, killing fourteen people; the players are hired — by competing interests — to find out whether it was negligence, design, or sabotage of Cadrex's own sabotage.
Crumble, the anonymous engineer, is dying and wants to go on record — but Cadrex's legal division has been hunting the identity for six years and is close.
A Tier 3 urban planning office offers the players a contract to assess the Gray Zone building stock; the assessment data, they realize, will be used to accelerate demolition rather than repair.
believers: Virtually all Tier 1 residents, Tier 2 labor advocates, independent structural engineers, the Gray Zone art collectives
evidence: Material degradation rates in Reclamation Block housing are documentably ahead of certification projections. Zoning reclassification records show 34 quiet amendments between 2193-2201 that are difficult to explain as routine updates. Cadrex disputes all findings and has successfully suppressed three independent audits through litigation.
